script: I couldn't give him cash—he exploded, demanding a manager, and everything changed.. I was in the register, scrolling through the morning stock list, when the first customer strutted in at exactly 9:00 AM, looking like he owned the place. He marched straight to the till and demanded a cash withdrawal. I said, "We can do cash‑back, but we only have cash from customers who've paid in cash." He was like, "What? How do you even know that?" He started shouting, "I need that cash now, or I am calling a manager!" I told him we had no money on hand yet because the till was empty—our store had just opened. He lost it, demanded a manager. The manager walked out, explained the same thing, and he stormed out, kicking a display plant like it was a personal vendetta. We thought the drama was over. Five minutes later, he bursts back in, holding a fire extinguisher like it was a weapon. He starts spraying the entire front staff with white powder, yelling that he's calling corporate, and then he just leaves. We're all standing there, covered in foam, stunned. It was only the beginning of the shift, and we just witnessed a grown man throw a temper tantrum, destroy a plant, and commit a literal felony before anyone even had their coffee.
